associations.rationale: For a highest-weight vector w, the displayed equality directly identifies E^k F^k w with a named polynomial in H applied to w; the separate natDegree theorem supplies the degree-k property.
This is only the type of the named polynomial and does not state the highest-weight-vector identity.
This theorem directly supplies the degree-k clause by stating that the polynomial used in the polynomial-action formula has natural degree k.
